title: Block: A Fixed-Size Sliding Window
oneLiner: Count the windows of exactly k elements whose sum reaches a target, updating the sum as the window slides.
keyTakeaway: A fixed window keeps one running sum: add the element entering, subtract the one leaving (index i - k). Build the first window before the loop.
explanation:
Return how many contiguous runs of exactly k elements have a sum of at least target. If k is longer than the array, there are none.

Sum nums[0..k-1] first. Then for each i from k to the end, add nums[i] and subtract nums[i - k]; each update is the next window. Check the first window and every slid one. Maximum Average Subarray and fixed-length anagram searches are this block.

starterCode.python:
def count_windows(nums, k, target):
    # 1. If k is longer than the array, no window fits: return 0.
    # 2. Sum the first k elements; that is the first window.
    # 3. Count it if it reaches the target.
    # 4. Slide: for each i from k to the end, add nums[i] and subtract nums[i - k], then check again.
    # 5. Return the count.

gotchas: Forgetting to check the very first window.
Subtracting nums[i - k + 1] instead of nums[i - k].

complexity.note: Each element enters and leaves the window once; only the running sum and count are kept.
